name: Madeira cake
origin: A dense, close-crumbed British loaf cake, historically served alongside a glass of Madeira wine (hence the name) though it does not itself contain wine; denser and less egg-rich than a Victoria sponge, with a firmer crumb that suits slow eating with a drink.

ingredients.note: grated lemon zest is the traditional Madeira cake flavouring; no zest substance record exists yet (see catalog.ts module notes)

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat softened butter and sugar until pale and fluffy

process.name: add eggs and zest
process.description: beat in eggs one at a time with the lemon zest

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: fold in flour, leavening and salt, mixing minimally for a close, firm crumb

process.name: bake
process.description: bake low and slow in a loaf or round tin

notes: Slightly less egg and sugar than a Victoria sponge (British baking references consistently describe Madeira as denser and firmer, with a lower proportion of raising agent), producing the close crumb the cake is known for. Ratios are representative of published British home-baking formulas rather than one single canonical source.
